page.title: Green dots and blog rows
page.kicker: Lecture 01 · week 1, day 1 · running case: an online/offline indicator, then a Medium-like blog
page.dek: Two builds on one page. First the green dot next to a user's name: what to store, who reports it, who deletes it, which store to pick and why six million heartbeats a minute make you pool connections. Then the rows of a blog: soft deletes, text columns, dates, and what a cache really is.
page.description: Lecture 01: design an online/offline indicator from heartbeats and TTLs, then make the everyday database and caching calls for a Medium-like blog.

chapters.title: How to approach a design
chapters.summary: Before any box: decide whether you are building outward from a known core or growing a day-zero design, and pick tools by the property you need, not the tool you like.

chapters.title: Green dots: the online/offline indicator
chapters.summary: Build the indicator one forced question at a time: what to store, how to read many users at once, who reports being alive, how long silence means offline, and who cleans up.

chapters.title: Redis or DynamoDB?
chapters.summary: Both give key-value access and a TTL, so speed is not the deciding question. Persistence, who runs it, lock-in, room to grow and how fast you learn about an expiry decide it.

chapters.title: Six million heartbeats a minute
chapters.summary: Storage was never the problem. Writes are. Why each tiny write spends most of its time opening a connection, how a pool fixes it, how to size one, and when it breaks.

chapters.title: Blog rows: database decisions
chapters.summary: A Medium-like blog has two plain tables. Every column hides a decision: whether delete means delete, where long text lives, and how to store a date.

chapters.title: What a cache is
chapters.summary: A cache is not “RAM” and not “Redis”. It is anything that saves an expensive disk read, network call or computation. One shared cache for the blog, a database table as a cache, and whether to compress.

chapters.title: What to keep
chapters.summary: The habits that ran through both builds, and where this lecture stops.
